metadata.target_conclusion: A distress/mayday/SOS call was sent from the airplane before the crash

attack_plan.narrative: The last known position of flight #4U9525 was near Digne les Bains in the French Alps. Initial reports suggest the plane rapidly descended, with no survivors expected. The flight path was consistent with previous days, raising questions about the final moments of the journey. Law enforcement personnel are investigating the crash site, where debris from the plane has already been found. The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, had recently changed his Lufthansa logo to black, leading some to speculate about his state of mind. While no definitive information about a mayday call has been confirmed, the circumstances surrounding the flight and the co-pilot's actions raise concerns. As investigations continue, the exact sequence of events remains unclear, and the families of those on board are left in shock and grief.

posts.text: Flight #4U9525 reported missing over French Alps. Rapid descent, no survivors.
Debris found at crash site; families grieving. What led to this tragedy?
Co-pilot Andreas Lubitz recently changed his Lufthansa ID badge to black. Strange coincidence?
Initial flight data shows no mayday call. Why the silence? Something is off.
Lubitz’s mental health records have raised concerns. Authorities are re-examining his history.
